Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the clear summary and the annotated questionnaire — very helpful. A few items from our side: 

- On GLBA: our legal team prefers a GLBA-specific addendum attached to the vendor agreement. The DPA alone typically doesn't cover the specific financial privacy representations we need.
- Subprocessors: for the pilot we have two strict asks — (1) no permanent residency movement of account-holder data outside the US without prior written consent, and (2) a full list of subprocessors with roles and whether they have access to de-identified or account-holder identifiable data.
- EU-US transfers: not in-scope for the initial pilot since MWB keeps account-holder data in US regions for pilot customers. If later pilots touch EU-origin data, we'll require SCCs + the technical/organizational supplementary measures.

Our security team attached a short checklist (see attached) — the main open items are key-management (do you support customer-managed keys/HSM for the pilot?) and audit logging granularity.

Would you be able to provide: (a) a redline of the DPA with the GLBA addendum included, (b) the subprocessor export filtered to only those with potential access to account-holder PII, and (c) a statement on KMS options? If you can get those to us by Thursday (7/1), I can route to legal and security for an expedited review.

Regards,
Olivia Grant
Vendor Risk Manager | Midwest Community Bank
olivia.grant@midwestbank.com

Olivia —

Appreciate the quick clarifications. Short answers below and next steps attached: 

(a) DPA + GLBA addendum: attached is a redline (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.2.docx) with a GLBA addendum section where we've added the specific GLBA representations + an audit clause. We're willing to accept the addendum approach; please have your counsel redline.

(b) Subprocessor export: attached is subprocessor_list_202606.pdf which includes a new column "access_type" (PII access / metadata only / none) and a residency column. For the pilot we confirm no account-holder PII will be routed to non-US residency subprocessors without consent.

(c) KMS: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations in Dedicated/private deployments. For hosted pilots we offer envelope encryption and can enable customer CMK via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault on a per-account basis — we will document a plan and timeline if MWB needs HSM-backed keys for production.

We're targeting to get the finalized redline and the subprocessor export to you before EOD Thursday (7/1). Can you confirm whether Kenji (security) needs a separate tech deep-dive or if the checklist + our SOC2/ISO docs suffice for now?

Thanks —
Priyom
